title: Use 2017 MacBook Pro to build a home Feiniu NAS
summary: A record of the painstaking efforts to build a Feiniu NAS using an idle 2017 MacBook Pro, from installing and booting to Ventoy boot, to discovering practical ways to mount cloud disks and project movies.
markdown:
![image]()
## Why choose to use MacBook to build NAS
I have a 2017 MacBook Pro at home that has been idle for a long time. To be honest, the performance is not bad, but it is a bit inadequate as a main machine. Rather than letting it eat ashes, it's better to do something with the waste heat.
I just happened to be researching NAS recently, and I was wondering if I could use this old Mac to build one. Compared with buying a finished NAS or assembling a dedicated server, the biggest advantage of using existing equipment is trial and error at zero cost - the equipment is there anyway, and you don't feel bad if it breaks.
In terms of system selection, I finally decided to use Feiniu fnOS. Mainly focus on two points:
- The interface is modern and easy to use (you don’t want to fiddle with the command line)
- Good support for domestic cloud disks (Baidu Netdisk and Alibaba Cloud Disk can be mounted)
### 2. Preparations before installation
Before starting, I first prepared these hardware:
- MacBook Pro 2017 (Protagonist)
- USB-C to Ethernet adapter (network stability is important)
- An 8GB USB flash drive (for making a boot disk)
- A 10TB hard drive (to store data)
The hardware is ready and I started searching for information. After searching online, I found that everyone basically uses a virtual machine solution - install a UTM virtual machine on MacOS, and then run Feiniu fnOS in the virtual machine.
But I don’t really want to take the path of virtual machines. I feel that if there is a layer of separation, the performance and experience will be compromised. My idea is: Can I install Feiniu fnOS directly on my MacBook, just like installing a Linux system?
With this idea in mind, I started my first attempt.
### 3. First installation attempt: pitfall experience
Following the tutorial on Feiniu’s official website, I did the following:
1. Downloaded the system image of Feiniu fnOS
1. Use Etcher to write the image to a USB flash drive and create a boot disk
1. Restart your MacBook and hold down the Option key to enter boot selection
1. Boot from the USB flash drive and follow the wizard to complete the installation
The entire installation process went very smoothly and was completed in about 30 minutes. The system prompted that the installation was successful. I happily unplugged the USB flash drive and restarted the computer.
Then... black screen.
After the computer starts up, the screen goes black and nothing is displayed. I thought it was because the startup items were not set properly, so I tried several more times, but still got the same result. Checking the BIOS settings, I found that the system was indeed installed, but it just wouldn't boot.
After struggling for a long time, I realized that the problem lies in the guidance method. Feiniu fnOS is installed, but the MacBook's bootloader cannot start it properly.
### 4. The ultimate solution: Ventoy boot startup
Just when I was about to give up, I accidentally saw someone mentioning the tool Ventoy.
![image]()
To put it simply, Ventoy is a multi-functional boot disk tool that can put multiple system images on the same USB disk and select them freely during startup. More importantly, it can not only boot the installation, but also boot the installed system.
I suddenly realized, doesn’t this just solve my problem? The system has been installed but cannot be started, then use Ventoy to boot it!
### Operation steps
1. Download Ventoy (https://www.ventoy.net)
1. Use Ventoy to recreate the USB flash drive (the USB flash drive will be formatted)
1. Copy the Feiniu fnOS image file directly to the USB drive
1. Plug in the USB flash drive and restart your MacBook
1. Select Feiniu System in Ventoy's boot menu
This time, it worked!
The system started successfully and entered the management interface of Feiniu fnOS. Although you have to plug in the USB disk every time you turn on the computer, at least it can be used. This is a staged victory.
### 5. First experience of the system: fresh interface
After successfully entering the system, the first feeling is: the interface is so fresh!
Compared with those traditional NAS systems, the UI design of Feiniu fnOS is very modern, a bit like using the management backend of a cloud service. The color scheme is comfortable, the icons are clear, and the operation logic is intuitive.
As you can see from the main interface, the system displays various operating statuses in real time:
- CPU usage, memory usage
- Network traffic (upload/download speed)
- Storage read and write speed
- System running time
My MacBook has no difficulty running Feiniu fnOS. The CPU usage is often around 45%, the memory is 5.2GB, and the system runs very smoothly.
![image]()
### 6. The function that impresses me the most
After using it for a period of time, there are a few features that particularly satisfy me.
### 1. Two-way backup function
This feature is really useful. It supports:
- *Local backup to cloud disk: **Automatically back up important files on NAS to Baidu Cloud Disk, Alibaba Cloud Disk, etc.
- *Back up cloud disk to local: **Synchronize files on cloud disk to local NAS
This achieves double insurance: one copy locally and one copy on the cloud, so you no longer have to worry about data loss.
### 2. Remotely mount cloud disk
This is the feature that surprises me the most! Feiniu fnOS supports direct mounting of domestic mainstream cloud disks. I mounted three:
![image]()
- Baidu Netdisk (SVIP member, 100GB)
- Alibaba Cloud Disk (8.73TB capacity)
- Quark network disk (6TB capacity)
After mounting, these cloud disks are just like local hard disks and can be operated directly. More importantly, you can directly transfer files between different cloud disks without having to download them locally and then upload them.
After comparing the speeds of the three companies, Quark Network Disk is obviously much faster. Whether uploading or downloading, Quark's speed is very stable and can almost fill up my bandwidth. Although Baidu Netdisk is SVIP, its speed is still not very good.
### 3. Photo album function
Feiniu fnOS has a built-in photo album management function that can automatically organize photos on your phone. After uploading, it will be automatically classified by time and location, making it easy to find photos.
The interface is also well done, and the browsing experience is close to that of professional photo album software. For people like me, whose mobile phone storage is often full, this feature is simply needed.
### 4. Film and television functions
The system comes with film and television library management. After putting movies and series into it, it will automatically recognize the information, download posters and introductions, and the display effect is very professional.
![image]()
This function is particularly useful to me, mainly for watching movies using the projector.
In the past, to watch movies, one had to either download the movie to a USB flash drive and plug it into the projector, or connect an HDMI cable to the computer. Not only is it troublesome, but the capacity of the USB flash drive is also limited and cannot hold several Blu-ray movies.
Now with Feiniu Film and Television, projection can directly access the film and television library on the NAS through the network. Lying on the sofa, you can select and play movies with the remote control. The experience is as convenient as a streaming media platform.
What's more, it's no problem to watch large-capacity Blu-ray movies. 40GB and 50GB movies can be streamed directly without lagging. The bandwidth of the Gigabit LAN is completely sufficient, and the picture quality and sound are original.
This method of use is really much more convenient than a USB flash drive. You can watch which movie you want without having to fetch files back and forth.
### 5. Natural UPS function
This feature is really an unexpected surprise! Using a MacBook to build a NAS has an advantage that no one would think of - the laptop battery is naturally a UPS uninterruptible power supply.
![image]()
Feiniu fnOS can perfectly identify the battery status of MacBook, which can be seen in the system:
- Current power supply type: Mains power supply
- Remaining power: 93%
- Connection status: normal connection
- You can set shutdown rules (such as automatic shutdown when the battery power drops below a certain level)
what does that mean? There is no need to panic when there is a power outage. The system automatically and seamlessly switches to battery power and the NAS continues to operate normally, data writing is uninterrupted and there is no risk of damage.
And if you use a desktop computer or an ordinary NAS server, if you want this function, you have to spend hundreds or even thousands of dollars to buy a UPS. Now with MacBook, this function comes built-in, so there is no need to invest extra at all.
For data security, this function is really important. If your home occasionally trips or loses power for repairs, you don’t have to worry at all. And the MacBook's battery can last for several hours, enough to wait for calls or manual shutdown.
This is a unique advantage of using a laptop to build a NAS compared to a desktop. It’s really ingenious.
### 7. Unexpected Discovery: New ways to play Quark Cloud Disk
After using it for a while, I discovered a magical operation of Quark Cloud Disk.
In the past, I used torrent files to download Blu-ray movies. Even with Thunder, the speed was extremely slow. A 40GB movie often takes a full day.
Now I found new method:
1. The seed file is first transferred to the Quark network disk (Quark supports offline downloading)
1. Quark is downloaded in the cloud at high speed (usually a few minutes)
1. High-speed download from Quark network disk to local NAS (full bandwidth)
Actual measurement results:
- Before: Using Thunder to download, the speed is 100-500 KB/s, and it takes 10+ hours to download a 40GB movie
- Now: Quark downloads offline for 5 minutes, then downloads from Quark to NAS, 100 Mbps bandwidth is full, 40GB takes about 1 hour
This method is not only fast, but also takes advantage of Quark’s 6TB large capacity to store frequently watched movies in the cloud disk so you can watch them at any time.
### 8. An episode about RAID
After the system was installed, I originally planned to buy another 10TB mechanical hard drive and form a RAID with the existing hard drive for data redundancy protection.
As a result, I checked the price on a certain website - the price of hard drives has increased!
The same 10TB mechanical disk is hundreds of dollars more expensive than when I bought it a few months ago. After thinking about it, although RAID is safe, for home NAS, regular backup to cloud disk is actually enough.
Therefore, this plan is temporarily shelved until the price drops. Anyway, the backup function of Feiniu fnOS can already ensure data security, which is not bad at this time.
### 9. Summary of use
After all this hard work, I still gained a lot:
1. Old equipment revitalized: 2017 MacBook Pro is more than enough to run NAS
1. Learned something new: Ventoy is a really easy to use tool that solves a big problem
1. Found practical functions: cloud disk mounting, two-way backup, new ways to download Quark
1. Saved a lot of money: no need to buy off-the-shelf NAS
After using it so far, the system has been running stably for more than 9 days (as you can see from the screenshots) without any problems. The CPU and memory usage are very healthy, and the temperature is also well controlled.
Who is it suitable for?
If you also have a spare MacBook (especially the x86 model around 2017) and want to build a home NAS, I think this solution is worth a try. The premise is:
- Willing to struggle (will encounter some pitfalls)
- Don’t mind plugging in a USB flash drive when booting (Ventoy boot)
- Want a NAS system with comprehensive functions and a beautiful interface?
Follow-up plan
- Continue to observe the system stability and see if there will be any problems in long-term operation.
- When hard disk prices come down, consider expanding the capacity or setting up a RAID.
- Study the Docker function of Feiniu fnOS and deploy some practical applications
- See if we can solve the Ventoy boot problem and achieve direct startup
Overall, this time is quite worth the hassle. An idle MacBook becomes a powerful home data center. This feeling of using old equipment is more fulfilling than buying new equipment.
